hypotheses.reasoning: The /search path is search-api -> catalog-svc -> third-party translation API (api.translate.example). The translation API first got slow at 02:54:30 (4.8s, #2524). From 02:55:29 on, its calls hung until the 30s timeout (#2672, #2902, #3052). search-api's calls to catalog-svc timed out at the same moments (#2675, #2903, #3053). Because those calls were held open, search-api's connection pool to catalog-svc filled (50/50, with the queue growing to 77) and web-bff returned 503s on GET /search from 02:57:51. The calls hung rather than failing fast, so this is dependency_timeout, not external_outage. Things I ruled out: the single circuit-breaker trip at 02:51 cleared and /search kept returning 200; the index-worker deploy at 02:52 isn't on the request path; metrics-agent and analytics-forwarder errors are telemetry noise; the status_v2 migration only breaks /checkout.
The translation provider may itself be down. But the logs only show hangs and timeouts, with no 5xx responses or refused connections.

A separate, concurrent incident: migration 0097 was half-applied (step 1 renamed the status_v2 column and committed, then step 2 hit a lock timeout and step 1 was not rolled back). That breaks order-service queries and /checkout, but not /search.

verdict.recommendedAction: Add a short timeout and a circuit breaker / fallback to catalog-svc's translation API calls: serve untranslated or cached text instead of blocking for 30s. Check the translation provider's status and open a ticket with them. Lower the search-api -> catalog-svc timeout so connections can't pile up. Separately, page the order-service owners to repair migration 0097: either rename status_v2_old back to status_v2, or finish the migration.
